Asian students in New Zeland language schools are dissatisfied with their learning experiences.

Asian students have negative perceptions of their learning experiences in New Zealand language school, because of their different cultural conceptualisations of learning and teaching.

the interplay between culture and language in the classroom.
the cultural dimension of classroom communication.
the cultural and pedagogical mismatch between the New Zealand teaching approaches and the Asian students’ expectations.

the mismatch between the teaching methods and students’ learning expectations in the New Zealand ESOL context has a negative impact on the learning experience of Asian students.
Asian students in the New Zealand English language classrooms are not learning what they want to learn.

the Asian students’ negative experience in the New Zealand language schools was due to the mismatch between their cultural learning conceptualisations and the interactive teaching approaches adopted by New Zealand language teachers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study provides a useful insight for New Zealand teachers into Asian students’ cultural learning conceptualisations, their perceptions of classroom communication and learning experiences.

the Asian students’ perceptions and experiences in New Zealand language classes are largely negative, and that there are some mismatches between Asian students’ learning concepts and New Zealand teachers’ teaching concepts.

we are not only teaching the language, but also the culture of the host country, so it is necessary to be aware of cultural differences and to make adjustments in teaching approaches to meet students’ learning needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
New Zealand teachers should be aware that Asian students’ learning styles and expectations are different from those of their New Zealand counterparts.
teachers need to be more aware of the different learning styles and expectations of students from diverse cultural backgrounds, and to adapt their teaching accordingly to meet students’ needs.
teachers need to be aware of their cultural and linguistic biases, and to develop the ability to reflect on and modify their teaching practices.
